description: Call transcripts with hand-labeled storyline excerpts for the meeting_linking prompt (ADR-013). Each case is one call: participants and transcript lines in the Littlebird shape (the owner's lines labeled, the other side often not). gold lists the excerpts that should be found: storyline, a line range the excerpt must overlap, and the stance. also_ok lists stances that are defensible for an ambiguous passage. Lines not covered by any gold excerpt should produce none. Used by scripts/eval_meeting_linking.py.
provenance: Synthetic. Patterns from the kinds of calls observed on a personal deployment (2026-11-05): client check-ins, process-automation calls, peer calls, cohorts. Names, firms and details invented. Labels authored with ADR-013 §4 and not independently reviewed; treat as a smoke test, not a benchmark.

storylines.name: What small firms actually adopt
storylines.thesis: Small firms adopt narrow, single-purpose AI tools that fit an existing workflow, not broad platforms or general assistants.

storylines.name: Local and open models
storylines.thesis: Private and sensitive workloads move to open models running on hardware the firm controls.

cases.title: Check-in with Dana
lines: Sam Rivera: Hey Dana, how's the office this week?
Busy, but good. Oh, we finally signed up for that intake-form tool, the one that only does client intake.
Sam Rivera: The narrow one? Nice.
Yeah, and honestly the front desk loves it. It replaced the clipboard in about a week.
Sam Rivera: I keep telling people that's where small firms land. The big suites are too much for a twelve-person office.
We did try the big suite last spring. Nobody opened it after the first month, so we cancelled.
Sam Rivera: Can you send me the login for the billing portal before Friday?
Sure, I'll send it tonight.

cases.title: Call with Lee
lines: Sam Rivera: How did the rollout go?
Lee Park: Better than I expected. We put the whole general assistant suite in front of all fourteen people, not just one task.
Lee Park: Three months in, everyone uses it every day, for drafting, scheduling, research, the lot.
Sam Rivera: That's not what I usually see at firms your size.
Lee Park: I know. I think it worked because we did a half-day training first.
Sam Rivera: Let's set up a time next week to look at the invoices.

cases.title: Peer call
lines: Sam Rivera: Anything new on your side?
Not much. A friend at another practice told me she read that small firms are all buying chatbots now.
Sam Rivera: Hm. Did her firm buy one?
No idea, she just read it somewhere.
Sam Rivera: Okay. Talk next week.

cases.title: Cohort session
lines: Welcome everyone, let's get started.
Sam Rivera: Quick data point from my own clients: of the five small firms I set up with the general copilot this year, three cancelled it within two months and kept only the receipt-scanning tool.
Interesting. Why the receipt tool?
Sam Rivera: It does one thing inside the bookkeeping they already do.
Sam Rivera: My bet is that this pattern holds for the next two years.
Thanks, let's take questions.

cases.title: Automation call with Ana
lines: Sam Rivera: Where did you land on the document review piece?
We moved it onto an open model running on the server in our back office. Our clients' contracts never leave the building now.
Sam Rivera: How's the quality compared to the hosted one?
A bit slower, but good enough, and our malpractice insurer was much happier.
Sam Rivera: I think that's where all the sensitive work ends up eventually.
By the way, did the parking validation get sorted?
Sam Rivera: Yes, it's on the front desk now.

cases.title: Access setup
lines: Sam Rivera: Did the VPN invite come through?
It did, I'm in.
Sam Rivera: Great. And the shared drive?
Still waiting on IT for that one. I'll ping them.
Sam Rivera: Thanks. Same time Thursday?
Works for me.

cases.title: Planning call
lines: Sam Rivera: What's next for you after tax season?
We're planning to try one of those agent platforms next quarter, the kind that does everything.
Sam Rivera: Want me to sit in on the demo?
Please. I'll send you the invite.
